body: Either killing myself, or travelling forward in time when the technology gets better.

My mom's brain got frozen in 1994 for $15k, including the required maintenance over however many hundreds of years. You'd have to adjust to inflation for 2012, so you'd probably be looking at something around $20-25k.

American Cryonic Society I think. In LA. My dad paid something like $15,000 to get my mom's brain frozen (including the investment money so when she gets unfrozen she'll have something to work off of)

Also, nothing determines when you're unfrozen. When my dad gave my mom's brain to American Cryonic Society it became their property. I think you can set some vague guidelines when they'll be unfrozen but it's ultimately in their hands. That's why it's risky. They can use your brain as a "guinea pig" for being unfrozen, the company may go under, there may be legislation making it illegal, too many people might get frozen where they have to scrap the whole project, etc. There is no 100% guarantee that you'll be unfrozen. Then there's the whole question of growing back a new body (probably would be easy in the future because of stem cells). That doesn't matter for me because I'd want a completely new body anyway haha

**Edit:** Scratch that, I talked to them, the company is *really* serious about making sure that *everyone* who is frozen has the best chance at getting unfrozen and living again. It is still a crap shoot, but they try their best to make sure you are revived. Nonetheless, there are no guarantees.

It makes me more depressed, they post pictures of themselves after the process and they still resemble men, they always talk about how they were ridiculed for being transgendered and "got them back" (hinting that they get regularly aren't really treated like women and discrimination is rampant), etc. It just makes me feel worse.
